text:
maria: heads-up — on main after the kernel-picker heuristics merge I'm seeing steady GPU resident growth on the 80GB nodes. starts around 12GB and drifts to ~18GB after a long run (no user-level leaks in app).

jonathan: reproable locally?

maria: yes on dev-gpu-03 with a long batch of small inferences (model=redwood-7b-uncased-quant). repro script attached below. growth only when kv_cache_enabled=true.

lee: can you paste nvidia-smi output and the allocator trace?

maria: here — run for ~1200 iters:

```
# repro run
REDWOOD_DEBUG_ALLOC=1 REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=1 python repro_mem_drift.py --model r7b --iters 1200 --batch 1
```

nvidia-smi (sample):
|  pid   | used GPU mem |
|  2345  | 12384 MiB    |
... after 1200 iters -> 18324 MiB

allocator trace snippet (from debug log):
```
[ALLOC] slab_alloc id=42 size=1048576 site=src/runtime/allocator.cpp:412
[FREE]  slab_free  id=42 site=src/runtime/allocator.cpp:421
[ALLOC] slab_alloc id=43 size=2097152 site=src/runtime/workspace.cpp:88
# repeated pattern, but many allocs never show FREE for id=43...47
```

asha: @maria can you confirm if this correlates with kernel selection path? iirc the heuristic changed to prefer tiled kernels for short sequences.

maria: good call — toggling KERNEL_PICKER_STRICT=1 (old behavior) removes the drift in quick runs. leaving new heuristic on produces the drift.

jonathan: that points to fragmentation vs true leak. if kernels pick different workspace sizes we might be doing many unique workspace allocations that fragment the slab pool. can you dump slab occupancy?

maria: added a small dump:

```
SLAB POOL SUMMARY:
pool_total=32768MB
pool_resident=18600MB
free_chunks=120
large_chunks=[8MB x 12, 16MB x 5, 32MB x 1]
internal_free_frag=~4MB avg
```

lee: hm free_chunks present but pool_resident still grows. could be that small chunks are leaking because their free lists are not updated when kernels free workspace. do we have callstack-enabled alloc traces?

maria: yes, sample backtrace on one leaked allocation:
```
# backtrace (most recent call last)
workspace_alloc at src/runtime/workspace.cpp:123
call_kernel at src/runtime/kernel_dispatch.cpp:78
generate_chunk at src/serving/inference_loop.cpp:210
```

asha: what's odd is the free should be symmetric. Maybe kernel returns a different pointer or uses an external buffer. Any recent change in kernel runtimes that switched to cudaMalloc for ephemeral buffers?

maria: search shows new tiled kernel path calls cudnnGetWorkspaceSize + cudaMalloc then memcpy in one code path. older path used preallocated workspace slices.

jonathan: bingo. that sounds like non-pooled allocations mixed with pooled allocations. If cudaMalloc is used and we don't track those to return them to the pool (or trim them), they appear as resident but untracked by slab free.

lee: two experiments: 1) force pooled-only path (disable tiled kernel or force prealloc) and 2) instrument to count external cudaMallocs.

maria: did both. external cudaMalloc count rose linearly with iterations when tiled path active. forcing pooled-only stabilized memory.

asha: mitigation options: revert kernel-picker change, or update tiled kernel to request workspace from global pool (use allocator->alloc_workspace(size) instead of cudaMalloc). Also add allocation accounting and a periodic trim/defrag call between requests.

jonathan: add a short-term patch that calls allocator->trim() every N requests to reclaim cudaMalloc'd memory if possible. long-term: unify workspace allocation interface so no path uses raw cudaMalloc.

maria: created patch branch: fix/tiled-workspace-pool (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321). patch replaces cudaMalloc with pool_alloc and adds ASSERT when unmatched free detected.

infra-bot: deploy-check: runtime/build (linux-gpu) passed — 1/7 jobs (lint) flagged warnings.

lee: can you run the perf benchmark with the patch and compare memory curve?

maria: ran 2h stress: resident stays flat ~12.2GB now. previous drift gone. CPU perf unchanged. KV hit ratio unaffected.

jonathan: great. what's the rollout plan? revert vs patch?

maria: plan: revert kernel-picker heuristic for now (short-term), merge fix/tiled-workspace-pool to main with tests, add allocator leak detector (alloc/free mismatch metrics) and add a canary to dedicated nodes to monitor memory over a week.

asha: also add a unit test for workspace path that asserts no raw cudaMalloc made (mock allocator).

lee: small suggestion — when kernel_picker picks a new kernel variant, we should attempt to reuse a compatible workspace slice (by rounding sizes), to avoid fragmentation. I'll open an issue.

maria: filed issue #987: "workspace-reuse-on-kernel-switch" with proposed heuristics.

jonathan: thanks all. next steps: merge hotfix revert, merge patch after review, schedule canary.

maria: attaching the repro script (short):
```
# repro_mem_drift.py (excerpt)
import time
from runtime_client import InferenceClient
c = InferenceClient(model='r7b')
for i in range(1200):
    res = c.generate('hello world')
    if i % 50 == 0:
        print(i, 'mem:', get_gpu_mem())
    time.sleep(0.01)
```

lee: nice, saved me a bunch of time. will review PR today.

asha: tagging @eng-sre for longer-term monitoring after canary. :eyes:

infra-bot: alert created: memory-drift-candidate on dev-gpu-03 (ID: md-20260318-01)

maria: thanks everyone. I'll follow up when PR merges and after canary run. :thumbsup:
